chapter.name: Grassroots Democracy -- Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas

questions.q: Sunita, a farmer in a small village, wants to raise a problem about her village's water supply with the Panchayati Raj body that is closest to the people in rural areas. Which body is that?
o: The Gram Panchayat of her village
The Panchayat Samiti of her block
The Zila Parishad of her district
The State Legislative Assembly
questions.a: The Gram Panchayat of her village: it is the base of the three tiers and the body closest to the people in rural areas.

questions.q: Meena says Panchayati Raj is a 'form of self-government'. All four statements below are true. Which one does the chapter give as the reason for calling the Panchayat system a form of self-government?
o: Panchayats bring governance closer to the people, so they can actively take part in decision-making
The Panchayati Raj system works at three levels: the village, the block and the district
Most Gram Panchayats are assisted by a Patwari who maintains the villagers' land records
The States have authority over the Panchayati Raj institutions
questions.a: Panchayats bring governance closer to the people, so they can actively take part in decision-making; the chapter says 'that is why' the Panchayat system is a form of self-government. The other statements are true but are not the reason given.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. Column A: 1. Gram Panchayat  2. Mandal Parishad  3. Zila Parishad  4. Gram Sabha. Column B: P. adults of a village who are enrolled as voters  Q. the council at the village level  R. the body at the district level  S. the body at the block level
questions.a: 1-Q, 2-S, 3-R, 4-P: the Gram Panchayat is the village council, the Mandal Parishad is another name for the block-level body, the Zila Parishad is the district-level body, and the Gram Sabha is the village's adults enrolled as voters.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Panchayats help to make sure that the benefits of government schemes reach the grassroots level. Reason (R): In recent years, more and more women have become Sarpanchs.
o: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A. The chapter names delivering scheme benefits to the grassroots as one of the Panchayats' vital roles, and it also says more and more women have become Sarpanchs; but the rise of women Sarpanchs is not the reason Panchayats carry scheme benefits to the grassroots.

questions.q: What is meant by the 'three-tier system' of Panchayati Raj? Name its three levels, starting from the bottom.
questions.a: Panchayati Raj works at three linked levels, so it is called a three-tier system. From the bottom up the levels are the village, the block and the district.
s: Meaning: the system works at three levels, hence 'three-tier'
Levels from the bottom up: village, block, district

questions.q: True or False? 'India has more towns and cities than villages.' Give the verdict and a reason.
questions.a: False. India has about 600,000 villages but only about 8,000 towns and over 4,000 cities, so villages far outnumber towns and cities.
s: Verdict: False
Reason: about 600,000 villages against about 8,000 towns and over 4,000 cities

questions.q: For each body below, name the level of Panchayati Raj it works at and the name of the body. (a) Kesarpura's own village council, which is deepening the village pond. (b) The body that is the link between Kesarpura's council and the body for the whole district. (c) The body at the top of the pyramid in Fig. 11.1.
questions.a: (a) Village level: the Gram Panchayat (Village Parishad). (b) Block level: the Panchayat Samiti (Block Panchayat or Mandal Parishad), the link between the Gram Panchayat and the Zila Parishad. (c) District level: the Zila Parishad (District Panchayat).
s: (a) Village level, Gram Panchayat
(b) Block level, Panchayat Samiti (Mandal Parishad)
(c) District level, Zila Parishad

questions.q: The chapter opens with Gandhi's words, 'The real India lives in its villages.' It then gives these figures: about 600,000 villages, 8,000 towns and over 4,000 cities, and a population of over 1.4 billion, almost two-thirds of whom live in rural areas. (a) About how many towns and cities does India have in all? (b) About how many villages are there for every town or city? (c) Do these figures support Gandhi's words? Give your verdict with a reason.
questions.a: (a) About 8,000 + 4,000 = 12,000 towns and cities (a little more, since there are over 4,000 cities). (b) 600,000 / 12,000 = about 50 villages for every town or city (a little fewer). (c) Yes. Villages outnumber towns and cities by about 50 to 1, and almost two-thirds of the people, about 93 crore of 140 crore, live in rural areas; so most Indians do live in villages.
s: (a) About 12,000 towns and cities
(b) About 50 villages for each town or city
(c) Yes: about 50 villages per town or city and almost two-thirds of the people rural

questions.q: Kotla, a village of about 900 people, faces three matters this month: (i) part of a farmer's harvested crop has been stolen from his field; (ii) several families who are entitled to a government housing scheme have not yet received its benefits; (iii) the village wants to start a weekly market so that its farmers can sell vegetables near home. The chapter says Panchayats address local issues, promote development and ensure that the benefits of government schemes reach the grassroots level. (a) to (c): Link each matter (i), (ii) and (iii) to a different one of these three roles, using each role once, and say how the Panchayat would help. (d) Explain why Kotla gains by handling these matters through its Panchayat rather than taking each one to the State capital.
questions.a: (a) The stolen crop is a local issue: the Panchayat can deal with it in the village, where the people and the fields are known (the chapter itself lists stolen crops among a village's questions). (b) The housing benefits are about government schemes reaching the grassroots: the Panchayat can see that the entitled families actually receive them. (c) The weekly market is development: the Panchayat can plan it so the village grows and farmers earn more. (d) The Panchayat is close to the people, so matters are settled quickly and the villagers themselves take part in the decisions; people cannot run to the State capital for every issue.
s: (a) Stolen crop = addressing a local issue, with how
(b) Housing benefits = benefits of schemes reaching the grassroots, with how
(c) Weekly market = promoting development, with how
(d) Panchayat is close to the people and lets them take part; cannot go to the capital for every issue

questions.q: Jaitpur is a farming village in the hills. Its main road was damaged by heavy rain. (a) The people of Jaitpur want to decide about repairing the road themselves. What is the system of local government in rural areas that lets them do so called? (b) What is the village council of Jaitpur called? (c) Who elects the members of this council? (d) Name the Panchayati Raj body at the district level, the top of the three tiers. (e) Give one reason why Jaitpur does not send this matter straight to the State capital.
questions.a: (a) Panchayati Raj (the Panchayat system). (b) The Gram Panchayat (Village Parishad). (c) The Gram Sabha, the adults of the village who are enrolled as voters. (d) The Zila Parishad (District Panchayat). (e) People cannot run to the State capital for every local issue; the Panchayat brings governance close to the people so they can decide such matters themselves.
s: (a) Panchayati Raj
(b) Gram Panchayat
(c) The Gram Sabha
(d) The Zila Parishad
(e) Cannot go to the capital for every issue; the Panchayat is close to the people

questions.q: Each Gram Panchayat elects a head or president. What is this head called?
o: The Sarpanch, also called the Pradhan
The Patwari, who keeps the land records
The Panchayat Secretary, who calls meetings
The Gram Sabha, which elects the members
questions.a: The Sarpanch, also called the Pradhan, is the head elected by each Gram Panchayat.

questions.q: Sonkhed wants to extend its primary school onto the plot next to it. Before it does, the Gram Panchayat must find out who owns that plot. Whose records should it consult?
o: The Patwari, who maintains the villagers' land records
The Panchayat Secretary, who calls the Panchayat's meetings
A Bal Panchayat member, who speaks for the children
The Zila Parishad member elected for the district
questions.a: The Patwari, who maintains the villagers' land records and in some cases keeps maps that are generations old.

questions.q: Read the statements about the village level of Panchayati Raj. I. The Gram Panchayat is the tier of Panchayati Raj that is closest to the people in rural areas. II. Most Gram Panchayats are also assisted by a Patwari, an officer who maintains the villagers' land records. III. Only the adults who hold a seat in the Gram Panchayat are members of the Gram Sabha. Which of these is/are correct?
o: I and II only
I and III only
II only
I, II and III
questions.a: I and II only. Statement III is wrong: the Gram Sabha is made up of all the adults of the village (or group of neighbouring villages) who are enrolled as voters, not only those who hold a Gram Panchayat seat.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Karan, a 16-year-old who lives in a village, is not a member of its Gram Sabha. Reason (R): The Gram Sabha is a group of adults from a village who are enrolled as voters.
o: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R explains A: the Gram Sabha is made up of adults enrolled as voters, and a 16-year-old is not an adult, so Karan is not a member.

questions.q: True or False? 'The Panchayat Secretary is not the head of the Gram Panchayat; the Secretary helps the Gram Panchayat with its administrative work.' Give the verdict and a reason.
questions.a: True. The head is the Sarpanch (Pradhan), elected by the Gram Panchayat; the Panchayat Secretary assists it with administrative functions such as calling meetings and maintaining records.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: the Sarpanch is the head; the Secretary calls meetings and maintains records

questions.q: What is the Gram Sabha? State one thing that its members do.
questions.a: The Gram Sabha is a group of adults from a village (or a group of neighbouring villages) who are enrolled as voters. Its members elect the Gram Panchayat directly; women and men in it also discuss all matters related to their area and take decisions.
s: Gram Sabha: adults of a village or group of neighbouring villages enrolled as voters
One thing: elect the Gram Panchayat, or discuss local matters and take decisions

questions.q: In 2026, Rekha became the first woman Sarpanch of her village. (a) Which change of recent years, described in the chapter, is her election a part of? (b) Name the provision, made at all three levels of Panchayati Raj, that makes sure women hold seats in the Gram Panchayat in the first place.
questions.a: (a) The chapter says that in recent years more and more women have become Sarpanchs; Rekha's election is part of this change. (b) The provision for reserving one-third of the seats for women.
s: (a) More and more women have become Sarpanchs in recent years
(b) One-third of the seats reserved for women

questions.q: Anjali claims: 'The Gram Sabha and the Gram Panchayat are the same body under two different names.' Test her claim against the chapter and give your verdict.
questions.a: Wrong. The Gram Sabha is the group of adults of a village (or group of neighbouring villages) who are enrolled as voters. The Gram Panchayat is the village council whose members are elected directly by the Gram Sabha. So one body is all the adult voters and the other is the council they elect; they are two different bodies.
s: Gram Sabha: the adults of a village or group of neighbouring villages enrolled as voters
Gram Panchayat: the village council whose members the Gram Sabha elects directly
Verdict: wrong; the voters elect the council, so they are two different bodies

questions.q:
The hamlets of Kolhi, Dhawa and Sirsi lie close together and share one Gram Sabha. Kolhi has 380 adults enrolled as voters, Dhawa 245 and Sirsi 175. This year these voters elected the 10 members of their Gram Panchayat: 5 from Kolhi, 3 from Dhawa and 2 from Sirsi. The Gram Panchayat then chose Shanti Devi of Sirsi to lead it.
(a) The chapter describes the Gram Sabha as a group of adults from a village. How can three hamlets have one Gram Sabha?
(b) How many members does this Gram Sabha have in all, and which hamlet has the most of them?
(c) Who elected the 10 members of the Gram Panchayat?
(d) What is the title of the post Shanti Devi now holds?
questions.a: (a) The chapter says a Gram Sabha is made up of the adults of a village or a group of neighbouring villages who are enrolled as voters, so neighbouring hamlets may share one. (b) 380 + 245 + 175 = 800 members; Kolhi has the most (380). (c) The Gram Sabha, the 800 adults enrolled as voters, elected them directly. (d) Sarpanch (or Pradhan).
s: (a) A Gram Sabha can cover a group of neighbouring villages
(b) 800 members; Kolhi has the most
(c) The Gram Sabha elected them directly
(d) Sarpanch or Pradhan

questions.q: Siraspur wants to dig a pond on a piece of common land near its fields. Explain the part each of these would play in the decision and the work: (a) the Gram Sabha; (b) the Gram Panchayat and its Sarpanch; (c) the Panchayat Secretary; (d) the Patwari. (e) The Patwari's records show two possible plots. Plot 1: 2 acres, common land, 600 m from the fields. Plot 2: 3 acres, 200 m from the fields, owned by four families who have not agreed to give it. The Sarpanch prefers Plot 2 because it is bigger and nearer. Which plot should the Gram Sabha choose? Decide, using the records.
questions.a: (a) The Gram Sabha, the village's adults enrolled as voters, discusses the pond and decides on it. (b) The Gram Panchayat, elected by the Gram Sabha, takes the work forward, led by the Sarpanch it elected as its head. (c) The Panchayat Secretary calls the meetings and keeps the records of the decisions. (d) The Patwari checks the land records, and perhaps old maps, to show which land is common land. (e) Plot 1. The village planned the pond on common land, and the records show only Plot 1 is common land; Plot 2 belongs to four families who have not agreed, so using it would take their land. Being bigger and nearer does not change who owns it, and the choice is the Gram Sabha's, not the Sarpanch's alone.
s: (a) Gram Sabha discusses and decides
(b) Gram Panchayat carries out the work, led by the Sarpanch it elected
(c) Secretary calls meetings and keeps records
(d) Patwari shows from land records which land is common land
(e) Plot 1: the records show only it is common land; Plot 2 belongs to families who have not agreed

questions.q: Which honour was Popatrao Baguji Pawar, the Sarpanch of Hiware Bazar, awarded in 2020?
o: The Padma Shri
The World's Children's Honorary Award
The child-friendly Gram Panchayat award
The Bharat Ratna
questions.a: The Padma Shri, awarded to Popatrao Pawar in 2020.

questions.q: Dnyaneshwar Kamble, Sarpanch of Tarangfal, follows the motto 'lok seva, gram seva'. What does it mean?
o: Service to the village is service to the public
The village must serve the State capital first
Every child in the village must go to school
Save the rain and plant a tree for every home
questions.a: 'Service to the village is service to the public.'

questions.q: Vandana Bahadur Maida became the first female Sarpanch of her village, Khankhandvi. In which State is Khankhandvi?
o: Madhya Pradesh
Maharashtra
Rajasthan
Sikkim
questions.a: Madhya Pradesh. (Tarangfal and Hiware Bazar, the other two Sarpanchs' villages, are in Maharashtra.)

questions.q: Read the statements about the chapter's exemplary Sarpanchs. I. Tarangfal and Hiware Bazar are both in Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra. II. Vandana Bahadur Maida, a member of the Bhil community, defied patriarchal norms to become the first female Sarpanch of her village. III. The model that Popatrao Pawar applied in Hiware Bazar included massive tree planting. Which of these is/are correct?
o: II and III only
I and II only
III only
I, II and III
questions.a: II and III only. Statement I is wrong: Hiware Bazar is in Ahmednagar district, but Tarangfal is in Solapur district (both are in Maharashtra).

questions.q: Who is Vandana Bahadur Maida? Name the two critical issues she addressed in her village.
questions.a: Vandana Bahadur Maida, of the Bhil community, defied patriarchal norms to become the first female Sarpanch of her village, Khankhandvi, in Madhya Pradesh. She addressed education and sanitation.
s: First female Sarpanch of Khankhandvi (Madhya Pradesh), from the Bhil community
Issues: education and sanitation

questions.q: A school magazine has two headlines for its page on village leaders: 'A barrier is broken' and 'A dry village turns green'. (a) Which Sarpanch story from the chapter fits each headline? (b) Give one fact from the chapter that supports each choice.
questions.a: (a) 'A barrier is broken' fits Dnyaneshwar Kamble (or Vandana Bahadur Maida); 'A dry village turns green' fits Popatrao Pawar of Hiware Bazar. (b) Kamble, a transgender person, was elected Sarpanch of Tarangfal (or Vandana defied patriarchal norms to become her village's first female Sarpanch); Hiware Bazar suffered frequent droughts but became green and prosperous after rainwater harvesting, watershed conservation and tree planting.
s: (a) Barrier: Kamble or Vandana Maida; green: Popatrao Pawar of Hiware Bazar
(b) A supporting fact for each headline

questions.q: Answer briefly about Hiware Bazar. (a) In which district and State is it? (b) Whose model of rainwater harvesting, watershed conservation and tree planting did its Sarpanch apply? (c) What did Hiware Bazar become within a few years?
questions.a: (a) Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra. (b) Anna Hazare's model. (c) A green and prosperous village.
s: (a) Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra
(b) Anna Hazare's model
(c) Green and prosperous

questions.q: Tenzin says: 'Of the chapter's three Sarpanchs, only Popatrao Pawar actually changed anything in the village; the other two are in the chapter only because they won elections.' Test his claim for each of the other two Sarpanchs and give your verdict.
questions.a: Wrong. Vandana Bahadur Maida changed things in her village: she convinced women to attend the Sabha meetings and addressed critical issues like education and sanitation, earning recognition far and wide. The claim says 'only' Pawar changed anything, so this one counter-example is enough to break it. Kamble is not in the chapter merely for winning either: his election as a transgender Sarpanch of Tarangfal, against six other candidates, under the motto 'service to the village is service to the public', itself changed who can lead a village. Verdict: the claim is wrong.
s: Vandana: brought women to the Sabha meetings and addressed education and sanitation, so she changed things
One counter-example breaks 'only', so the claim is wrong
Kamble: a transgender person elected Sarpanch against six candidates, itself a change in who can lead; verdict wrong

questions.q:
Rukmini, a woman of the Bhil community, became the first female Sarpanch of Sakhli. Few women came to the Sabha meetings, so before the next meeting she tried a different step in each of two wards. Ward 1 has 120 women voters: she sent a written notice to every home, and the number of women attending went from 12 to 18. Ward 2 has 140 women voters: she visited the homes and talked with the women, and the number attending went from 14 to 84.
(a) Which Sarpanch in the chapter does Rukmini's story follow most closely, and in which State is that Sarpanch's village?
(b) What percentage of each ward's women voters came to the meeting after Rukmini's step?
(c) In Ward 2, how many times as many women came after the visits as before?
(d) Rukmini can use only one of the two steps in the other wards. Which should she use? Decide, using the data and what the chapter says Vandana did.
questions.a: (a) Vandana Bahadur Maida, the first female Sarpanch of Khankhandvi, in Madhya Pradesh. (b) Ward 1: 18 / 120 x 100 = 15%. Ward 2: 84 / 140 x 100 = 60%. (c) 84 / 14 = 6 times. (d) Home visits. They brought 60% of the women voters against 15% for notices (attendance rose 6 times, against 1.5 times with notices), and this matches the chapter: Vandana convinced the women of her village to attend the Sabha meetings.
s: (a) Vandana Bahadur Maida; Madhya Pradesh
(b) Ward 1: 15%; Ward 2: 60%
(c) 6 times
(d) Home visits: 60% against 15%, and Vandana convinced the women to attend

questions.q: A district poster will show one of the chapter's three Sarpanchs under the title 'Results that lasted', meaning a Sarpanch whose work, as the chapter describes it, left a lasting change in the village. (a) to (c): Weigh Dnyaneshwar Kamble, Vandana Bahadur Maida and Popatrao Pawar against this title, one fact each. (d) Choose one for the poster and give your main reason. (e) Name the strongest point for one Sarpanch you did not choose.
questions.a: (a) Kamble: the chapter tells of his election in 2017 against six other candidates and his motto of service, but it describes no particular result of his work, so it gives the least evidence for this title. (b) Vandana Maida: she brought the village's women to the Sabha meetings and addressed education and sanitation, earning recognition far and wide; a real change, though the chapter gives no picture of the village afterwards. (c) Pawar: Hiware Bazar, once hit by frequent droughts and poor yields, became green and prosperous in a few years as groundwater was recharged, and he was awarded the Padma Shri in 2020. (d) Best choice: Pawar, because the chapter shows the end result, a drought-hit village that became green and prosperous (Vandana is acceptable if argued from the lasting effect of bringing women into decisions). (e) For example: Vandana changed who takes part in the village's decisions; or Kamble's election showed that a transgender person can lead a village.
s: (a) Kamble weighed: election and motto, but no result of his work described
(b) Vandana weighed: women at Sabha meetings, education and sanitation
(c) Pawar weighed: drought-hit village became green and prosperous; groundwater recharged
(d) A reasoned choice (Pawar best; Vandana acceptable with reason)
(e) Strongest point for a Sarpanch not chosen

questions.q: Under the Child-Friendly Panchayat Initiative, in which forums do children take part on a regular basis?
o: Bal Sabhas and Bal Panchayats
Gram Sabhas and Gram Panchayats
Panchayat Samitis and Zila Parishads
Sangrahanas and karvatikas
questions.a: Bal Sabhas and Bal Panchayats, where children raise their concerns while village elders try to find solutions.

questions.q: Rajasthan's 'Children's Parliament' began as an offshoot of which initiative?
o: Bunker Roy's 'Barefoot College'
Anna Hazare's watershed model
The Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat
The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
questions.a: Bunker Roy's 'Barefoot College' initiative, a few decades ago.

questions.q: In Rajasthan's Children's Parliament, the elected representatives formed a 'Cabinet'. What did the Cabinet do?
o: It oversaw school management and spoke up for community needs
It kept the land records and the generations-old maps of all the villages
It elected the Sarpanch of each Gram Panchayat in the area
It built compound walls and kitchens for the schools
questions.a: It oversaw school management and advocated for community needs.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat in west Sikkim has been declared a child-friendly Gram Panchayat. Reason (R): A few Bal Panchayats in Maharashtra have worked to eliminate child labour and child marriage.
o: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A. Sangkhu Radhu Khandu was declared child-friendly for its own work in Sikkim (compound walls for schools and kitchens for hygienic mid-day meals); the work against child labour and child marriage was done by Bal Panchayats in Maharashtra, a different example.

questions.q: True or False? 'The Child-Friendly Panchayat Initiative is found only in Rajasthan.' Give the verdict and a reason.
questions.a: False. The chapter says steps are being taken in several States; besides Rajasthan's Children's Parliament it gives examples from Maharashtra (Bal Panchayats) and Sikkim (Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat).
s: Verdict: False
Reason: several States, e.g. Maharashtra and Sikkim as well as Rajasthan

questions.q: (a) Name two formal procedures that Rajasthan's Children's Parliament followed, as real elections do. (b) Why would taking part in these teach children more about democracy than only reading about it?
questions.a: (a) Voter ID cards and campaigning (in parliament-like elections). (b) The children actually voted, campaigned and then, as elected representatives, ran a Cabinet that oversaw school management, so they learned democracy and social responsibility by doing it, not only by hearing about it.
s: (a) Voter ID cards and campaigning
(b) Learning by doing: they voted, campaigned and governed through the Cabinet

questions.q: Answer briefly about the Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat. (a) In which part of which State is it? (b) What did it build so that school buildings are safer for children? (c) What did it build so that students get hygienically cooked mid-day meals?
questions.a: (a) West Sikkim. (b) Compound walls for the schools. (c) Kitchens in the schools.
s: (a) West Sikkim
(b) Compound walls for schools
(c) Kitchens in the schools

questions.q: Write a short situation (two or three sentences) in which the Bal Sabha of a village raises a concern of the children and the village elders act on it. Then explain how your situation shows what the Child-Friendly Panchayat Initiative is meant to do.
questions.a: Sample: 'At the Bal Sabha of Dhanora, the children said the path to school floods every monsoon and they miss classes. The Sarpanch and the elders listened and decided to raise the path before the next rains.' This shows the Initiative's aim: children get a chance to express their opinions on matters that concern their wellbeing, Panchayats listen to everyone's voice including children's, and the elders try to find solutions.
s: A situation in which children raise a real concern in a Bal Sabha or Bal Panchayat
Village elders act on it
Link to the aim: children's voice on their wellbeing heard, elders find solutions

questions.q: A visiting officer wants to know how the Child-Friendly Panchayat Initiative has helped children. For each need in (a) to (c), name the example from the chapter that meets it and say what was done. (a) Children who had left school. (b) Safety of children at school. (c) Clean, healthy school food. (d) Compare your examples: in which of them did children themselves do the work, and in which did the Gram Panchayat's adults do it?
questions.a: (a) The Bal Panchayats of Maharashtra: members convinced parents and other adults to send children back to school and not to arrange marriages for girls who should be studying; they brought many children back to school. (b) Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat, west Sikkim: it built compound walls for schools. (c) The same Gram Panchayat built kitchens in schools so mid-day meals are hygienically cooked. (d) In (a) the children themselves, as Bal Panchayat members, did the work; in (b) and (c) the work was done by the Gram Panchayat, the adults, for the children.
s: (a) Maharashtra's Bal Panchayats brought children back to school
(b) Sangkhu Radhu Khandu built school compound walls
(c) Sangkhu Radhu Khandu built school kitchens for hygienic mid-day meals
(d) Children did the work in (a); the Gram Panchayat's adults in (b) and (c)

questions.q:
The Bal Panchayat of Wadgaon, a village in Maharashtra, keeps a register. Last year its members visited the families of 20 children who were working instead of going to school, and 12 of those children went back to school. They also visited the families of 10 girls whose marriages were being arranged although the girls should have been studying; 8 of those marriages were called off and the girls stayed in school. This year the register lists 15 families of each kind, but the members have time for only 10 visits before the school term begins.
(a) Name the two practices that the chapter says a few Bal Panchayats in Maharashtra have worked to eliminate.
(b) What percentage of last year's visits succeeded in each group?
(c) According to the chapter, whom do the Bal Panchayat members try to convince, and of what?
(d) If this year's visits succeed at last year's rates, where should the 10 visits go to keep the most children in school? Show the working.
questions.a: (a) Child labour and child marriage. (b) Working children: 12 / 20 x 100 = 60%. Girls: 8 / 10 x 100 = 80%. (c) Parents and other adults: to send their wards back to school, and not to arrange marriages for girls who should be studying. (d) To the girls' families. 10 visits x 80% = 8 children kept in school, against 10 x 60% = 6 if the visits go to working children's families; any mix gives between 6 and 8, so all 10 to the girls' families keeps the most.
s: (a) Child labour and child marriage
(c) Parents and other adults: send wards back to school, do not arrange marriages for girls who should study
(d) Girls' families: 8 children against 6

questions.q: Which government scheme named in the chapter promotes the construction of all-weather roads in rural areas?
o: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
The Child-Friendly Panchayat Initiative
The Barefoot College initiative
Anna Hazare's watershed model
questions.a: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana.

questions.q: A Gram Panchayat has 15 seats. It follows the provision for women that the chapter describes for all three levels of Panchayati Raj. How many of its seats are reserved for women?
questions.a: 5 seats: one-third of 15 is 5.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. Column A: 1. Panchayat Samiti  2. Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana  3. Special rules at all three levels  4. The States' authority over Panchayati Raj. Column B: P. structure and functions differ a little from State to State  Q. the link between the Gram Panchayat and the Zila Parishad  R. all-weather roads in rural areas  S. the needs of disadvantaged sections are heard
questions.a: 1-Q, 2-R, 3-S, 4-P: the Panchayat Samiti links the Gram Panchayat and the Zila Parishad; the Yojana promotes all-weather rural roads; the special rules help disadvantaged sections be heard; because States have authority over them, the institutions differ a little across States.

questions.q: Read the statements about the block and district levels. I. Besides the members elected by the local people, a Panchayat Samiti may have local members of the State Legislative Assembly among its members. II. The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana promotes the construction of all-weather roads in rural areas. III. The provision for reserving one-third of the seats for women applies at the block and district levels too, not only in the Gram Panchayat. Which of these is/are correct?
o: I, II and III
I and II only
II and III only
I only
questions.a: I, II and III. The chapter says these bodies may have other members such as Sarpanchs and local members of the State Legislative Assembly; that the Yojana promotes all-weather roads in rural areas; and that the institutions at all three levels have a provision for reserving one-third of the seats for women.

questions.q: Why is the Panchayat Samiti called the link between the Gram Panchayat and the Zila Parishad? Give one task it does as this link.
questions.a: It works at the block level, between the Gram Panchayats of the villages below and the Zila Parishad of the district above. As the link it coordinates matters across Gram Panchayats, for example by collecting the development plans of all the Gram Panchayats and putting them together to present at the District or State level.
s: It sits at the block level, between the village and district levels
Task: collects and combines the Gram Panchayats' development plans to present at the district or State level

questions.q: State the two special provisions that the chapter says have been made at all three levels of Panchayati Raj.
questions.a: (1) One-third of the seats are reserved for women. (2) Special rules have been made so that disadvantaged sections of the population can make their needs and problems heard.
s: One-third of seats reserved for women
Special rules so disadvantaged sections can make their needs heard

questions.q: The Gram Panchayat of Chandpur wants an all-weather road to join the village to the block's market. (a) Under which government scheme named in the chapter could the funds come? (b) Trace the path Chandpur's road plan takes before funds can be allotted.
questions.a: (a) The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana. (b) The Gram Panchayat prepares the plan; the Panchayat Samiti collects it with the plans of all the other Gram Panchayats of the block and puts them together; the combined plan is presented at the District or State level, which makes the allotment of funds easier.
s: (a) Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
(b) Gram Panchayat plan, then Panchayat Samiti combines plans, then presented at district or State level for funds

questions.q: Pahadganj block has 18 Gram Panchayats. This year 12 of them sent their development plans to the Panchayat Samiti on time; the other 6 prepared no plan at all. (a) What does the Panchayat Samiti do with the 12 plans? (b) Explain, step by step, what the 6 villages are likely to lose. (c) Suggest one step the Samiti could take before next year that fits its role.
questions.a: (a) It puts the 12 plans together and presents them at the District or State level. (b) The combined plan is what makes the allotment of funds for development projects and schemes such as the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana easier; the needs of the 6 villages are not in it, so they are less likely to get funds this year, and their roads or other works may wait. (c) Since its role is to coordinate matters across Gram Panchayats, it could remind and help the 6 Gram Panchayats to prepare their plans in time.
s: (a) Combines the plans and presents them at the district or State level
(b) Chain: combined plan helps allot funds; the 6 villages' needs are missing, so they may get no funds
(c) A step that fits its coordinating role, e.g. helping the 6 Gram Panchayats prepare plans

questions.q:
Devgarh block has 24 Gram Panchayats. The Panchayati Raj body of the block has 31 members. Of these, 24 are elected to it by the local people; the others are 6 Sarpanchs of villages in the area and the local member of the State Legislative Assembly. The body works between the Gram Panchayats of the block and the body for the whole district.
(a) What is this block-level body called?
(b) How many of its 31 members sit in it because of another post they hold, not because the local people elected them to this body?
(c) Name the Panchayati Raj body at the district level, above it.
(d) Name one special provision that the chapter says this body, like the bodies at the other two levels, must have.
questions.a: (a) The Panchayat Samiti (also called the Block Panchayat or Mandal Parishad). (b) 6 Sarpanchs + 1 member of the State Legislative Assembly = 7 members (31 - 24 = 7). (c) The Zila Parishad (District Panchayat). (d) Either: one-third of the seats reserved for women; or special rules so that disadvantaged sections of the population can make their needs and problems heard.
s: (a) Panchayat Samiti
(b) 7 members
(c) Zila Parishad
(d) One-third seats for women, or special rules for disadvantaged sections

questions.q: At a hearing held under the special rules for disadvantaged sections, the Panchayat Samiti of Kalimpur block hears two requests. It can pay for only one from its own funds this year. Hamlet R: 45 families, all from a disadvantaged section; a stream with no bridge cuts it off from the school 2 km away, and in the monsoon 30 of its 50 school children miss school for about six weeks. It asks for a footbridge. Hamlet S: 120 families, 20 of them from a disadvantaged section; it asks for its muddy 3 km path to the main road to be made an all-weather road. (a) What are the special rules behind this hearing meant for, and at which levels of Panchayati Raj have they been made? (b) What percentage of Hamlet R's school children miss school in the monsoon? (c) Which government scheme named in the chapter could fund Hamlet S's request instead, and what does it promote? (d) The two hamlets belong to different Gram Panchayats. Why is the Panchayat Samiti the right body to weigh the two requests? (e) Which request should the Samiti pay for from its own funds? Decide, using the data and your answers to (a) and (c).
questions.a: (a) They are meant to let disadvantaged sections of the population make their needs and problems heard; they have been made at all three levels (village, block and district). (b) 30 / 50 x 100 = 60%. (c) The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, which promotes the construction of all-weather roads in rural areas. (d) The Panchayat Samiti coordinates matters across Gram Panchayats; it is the block-level link between them and the Zila Parishad, so it can weigh requests from two different Gram Panchayats. (e) Hamlet R's footbridge. All 45 of its families are from a disadvantaged section (against 20 of 120 in S), 60% of its children lose about six weeks of school, and the hearing exists so that such needs are heard; Hamlet S's road is the kind of work the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana is meant for, so it can seek those funds instead.
s: (a) Let disadvantaged sections make their needs heard; all three levels
(c) Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, for all-weather rural roads
(d) The Samiti coordinates matters across Gram Panchayats as the block-level link
(e) Hamlet R: all families disadvantaged, 60% of children miss school, S can seek scheme funds

questions.q: In the Arthashastra passage quoted in the chapter, what is a 'sangrahana'?
o: A sub-district headquarters
A district headquarters
A provincial headquarters
A village council
questions.a: A sub-district headquarters, set up for every 10 villages.

questions.q: Kautilya's Arthashastra explains how a whole administrative structure should be put in place. Between which two ends does this structure run?
o: From the village to the regional capital
From the district to the national capital
From the block to the district
From the Gram Sabha to the Zila Parishad
questions.a: From the village to the regional capital.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Under Kautilya's plan, the villages served by one dronamukha would hold eight karvatikas. Reason (R): The Arthashastra passage sets a karvatika for every 100 villages and a dronamukha for every 400 villages.
o: A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
questions.a: A is false, but R is true. R quotes the passage correctly, and by it a dronamukha's 400 villages hold 400 / 100 = 4 karvatikas, not eight.

questions.q: State any two of the points the chapter makes in its closing summary about local government in rural areas.
questions.a: Any two of: (1) local government in rural areas is organised into a three-tier system; (2) democracy in the Panchayati Raj system works both through direct participation of people and through their elected representatives; (3) the Panchayati Raj institutions give people in rural areas a measure of self-governance, so they may manage their issues and collaborate in development plans.
s: First point of the summary
Second point of the summary

questions.q: The Arthashastra sets a sangrahana for every 10 villages, a karvatika for every 100, a dronamukha for every 400 and a sthaniya for every 800. (a) How many times as many villages does a sthaniya serve as a karvatika? (b) Between which two units next to each other in this list is the jump in villages the biggest, counted in 'times'?
questions.a: (a) 800 / 100 = 8 times. (b) From the sangrahana to the karvatika: 10 to 100 is 10 times, while 100 to 400 is 4 times and 400 to 800 is only 2 times.
s: (a) 8 times
(b) Sangrahana to karvatika (10 times, against 4 and 2 times)

questions.q: Answer briefly about the Arthashastra. (a) Who wrote it, and about how long ago? (b) Name two things it describes besides village administration. (c) What did it say the king should set up for every 800 villages?
questions.a: (a) Kautilya (later also known as Chanakya), some 2,300 years ago. (b) Any two of: how a state should be structured and run, how the economy can be made prosperous, the duties of the ruler, how to conduct war. (c) A sthaniya, a provincial headquarters.
s: (a) Kautilya (Chanakya), about 2,300 years ago
(b) Any two of: running a state, a prosperous economy, the ruler's duties, conducting war
(c) A sthaniya (provincial headquarters)

questions.q: The chapter is titled 'Grassroots Democracy'. Give three pieces of evidence from the chapter that show why this title fits the Panchayati Raj system, explaining each in a line.
questions.a: Any three, each explained: (1) the Gram Sabha, all the adults of a village enrolled as voters, discuss matters and take decisions themselves, so democracy starts at the very bottom; (2) the Gram Panchayat, closest to the people, is elected directly by the Gram Sabha; (3) Panchayats make sure the benefits of government schemes reach the grassroots level; (4) one-third of seats are reserved for women and special rules let disadvantaged sections be heard; (5) through Bal Sabhas and Bal Panchayats even children's voices are heard.
s: First piece of evidence with explanation
Second piece of evidence with explanation
Third piece of evidence with explanation

questions.q: Read four events from the imaginary village of Moti Nagar. For each, name the point of the chapter's closing summary that it shows best, using each point once: the three-tier system, direct participation, elected representatives, or self-governance. (a) At a Gram Sabha meeting, the women and men of Moti Nagar who are enrolled as voters discussed where street lights were needed and voted for the main lane. (b) The Gram Panchayat members whom they had elected bought the lights and saw that they were put up. (c) Moti Nagar's Gram Panchayat works under a Panchayat Samiti for its block and a Zila Parishad for its district. (d) Moti Nagar dealt with its dark lanes through its own Panchayat, without waiting for the State capital, and also joined its neighbouring villages in a shared development plan.
questions.a: (a) Direct participation: the people themselves discussed and decided in the Gram Sabha. (b) Elected representatives: the members the people elected acted for them. (c) The three-tier system: village, block and district. (d) Self-governance: the village managed its own issue and collaborated in development plans.
s: (a) Direct participation
(b) Elected representatives
(c) Three-tier system
(d) Self-governance

questions.q:
A district today has about 1,200 villages. They are served by 410 Gram Panchayats (some of them cover a group of neighbouring villages), 9 Panchayat Samitis and 1 Zila Parishad. A student project compares this with the Arthashastra's rule: a sangrahana for every 10 villages, a karvatika (district headquarters) for every 100, a dronamukha for every 400 and a sthaniya for every 800.
(a) On average, about how many villages does each Gram Panchayat serve, and about how many does each Panchayat Samiti serve?
(b) Which of Kautilya's four units is closest in size, by villages served, to today's Panchayat Samiti in this district?
(c) About how many Gram Panchayats does each Panchayat Samiti link to the Zila Parishad, on average?
(d) A student says: 'This district's one Zila Parishad serves as many villages as more than ten of Kautilya's district headquarters.' Using the data, is she right?
questions.a: (a) 1,200 / 410 = about 2.9, so about 3 villages per Gram Panchayat; 1,200 / 9 = about 133 villages per Panchayat Samiti. (b) The karvatika (100 villages): 133 is much nearer to 100 than to 10 (sangrahana) or 400 (dronamukha). (c) 410 / 9 = about 46 Gram Panchayats per Panchayat Samiti. (d) Yes. The Zila Parishad serves all 1,200 villages, and a karvatika, Kautilya's district headquarters, serves 100, so it covers 1,200 / 100 = 12 karvatikas' worth of villages, which is more than ten.
s: (a) About 3 villages per Gram Panchayat; about 133 per Panchayat Samiti
(b) The karvatika (100 villages)
(c) About 46 Gram Panchayats per Samiti
(d) Yes: 1,200 / 100 = 12 karvatikas, more than ten

questions.q: Your class holds a mock Gram Sabha for an imaginary village, Sundarpur, which has 1,180 adults enrolled as voters. Two proposals are before it. Proposal X: an all-weather road joining Sundarpur to the highway 5 km away. Proposal Y: a compound wall and a kitchen for the village school, whose 160 pupils eat mid-day meals cooked in the open and whose yard opens straight onto a busy lane. (a) Who may take part in the decision? (b) The children of Sundarpur also want to give their views. Through which forums does the chapter say children can take part? (c) Which proposal could get funds through a government scheme named in the chapter, and what does that scheme promote? (d) Which example from the chapter supports Proposal Y, and what was that Gram Panchayat declared? (e) Which proposal should Sundarpur take up first? Give a reasoned judgement.
questions.a: (a) The Gram Sabha: Sundarpur's 1,180 adults enrolled as voters. (b) Bal Sabhas and Bal Panchayats, under the Child-Friendly Panchayat Initiative. (c) Proposal X, under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, which promotes the construction of all-weather roads in rural areas. (d) The Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat in west Sikkim, which built compound walls for schools and kitchens for hygienic mid-day meals; it was declared a child-friendly Gram Panchayat. (e) Either, with reasons: Y first, because it protects 160 children every day and the village can act on it itself, while X can seek funds under the scheme; or X first, because a road links the whole village to markets and services. A strong answer weighs who benefits, how soon, and where the money can come from.
s: (a) The Gram Sabha, the 1,180 adult voters
(b) Bal Sabhas and Bal Panchayats
(c) Proposal X; Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana for all-weather rural roads
(d) Sangkhu Radhu Khandu, declared a child-friendly Gram Panchayat
(e) A reasoned judgement weighing both proposals
